# chemaclass/edifact-parser

> A PHP toolkit for UN/EDIFACT: parse, write, validate and stream EDI interchanges with a
> typed, object-oriented API. PHP 8.0+, PSR-4, no required runtime dependency beyond
> `sabas/edifact` and `webmozart/assert`.

Install with `composer require chemaclass/edifact-parser`. Entry point is
`EdifactParser::createWithDefaultSegments()->parse($string)` or `->parseFile($path)`,
which returns a `ParserResult`.

Every snippet in these documents exists as a runnable file under `example/`, and CI runs
them — so they cannot silently rot.

## Docs

- [Parsing](docs/llms/parsing.md): EdifactParser, ParserResult, tokenizers, streaming
- [Reading data](docs/llms/reading.md): typed accessors, keyed lookups, query API, line items, contexts
- [Writing](docs/llms/writing.md): segment builders, serializer, full interchange assembly
- [Validation](docs/llms/validation.md): rule sets, violations, diagnostics
- [Extending](docs/llms/extending.md): custom segments, grouping rules, tokenizers, introspection
- [CLI](docs/llms/cli.md): the `edifact` binary, output contract, exit codes

## Gotchas

Things that are not guessable from the signatures, and that have bitten people:

- **Keyed lookups return the typed segment, not a context.** `segmentByTagAndSubId('NAD','BY')`
  is a `NADNameAddress`, so accessors and `instanceof` work. To reach what was grouped under
  it, use `$message->childrenOf($segment)` or `contextFor($segment)`. (Before 7.0 this
  returned a `ContextSegment` and every typed accessor was a fatal error.)
- **Numeric-looking subIds are int array keys.** PHP normalizes `'1'` and `'21'`, so keyed
  maps are `array<string, array<array-key, SegmentInterface>>` and `segmentByTagAndSubId()`
  accepts `string|int`.
- **Unknown tags never throw.** They become `UnknownSegment`, still readable via
  `rawValues()`. Absence of a segment is `null`, not an exception — always null-check.
- **Keyed views keep the last duplicate.** Two segments sharing tag+subId collapse in
  `allSegments()`/`segmentsByTag()`. Use `query()` or `segments()` when duplicates matter;
  both preserve order and every occurrence.
- **`NativeTokenizer` is the default since 7.0.** `SabasTokenizer` is still available but
  strips every byte in `\x80-\xFF`, destroying non-ASCII data.
- **Match on diagnostic codes, never on messages.** `DiagnosticCode` values are public API;
  the human-readable text is not.
- **Grouping is heuristic, not directory-driven.** `GroupingRules` approximates segment
  groups with a configurable parent/child tag list; it is not the UNTDID structure.
